record_reviews.summary: Catherine and Caroline report family news, the birth of Fanny Biddulph’s son, Emma’s social life and opinions on Darwin’s book, financial instructions about Robarts dividends, and a confidential hearsay story about FitzRoy and Captain White.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied single day [16 Feb 1837]; the header says Thursday Night.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Joint incoming letter: Catherine writes pp.1–4, Caroline adds p.6 and signs p.7. The FitzRoy account is explicitly hearsay relayed through an apothecary and is not established fact.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Acknowledges Darwin’s last letter and supplies family/social information; no specific surviving Darwin prompt is located. Darwin’s last letter is mentioned but not preserved; a reply is not identifiable from this family news letter.

evidence.quote: we were very glad to have your last letter
I hope Charles will rather risk a little repetition
this is the kind of story the apothecary heard

record_reviews.summary: Treasury minutes record the Chancellor’s recommendation and the Board’s sanction of up to £1000 to support Darwin’s illustrated natural-history publication, subject to an approved plan and progress certificates.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Safe single XML day 25 August 1837.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Corporate Board minute; the Chancellor and Lords Commissioners are institutional voices, with no individual Darwin voice. The undated memorandum in the footnote is contextual, not body text.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: The 31 August Spearman letter executes this minute’s instruction to communicate the Board’s views to Darwin; it is a distinct official follow-on, not a Darwin response.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Institutional decision that prompts the official communication 377; not itself a Darwin-authored prompt. The minutes explicitly direct an immediate communication to Darwin, and 377 supplies that communication.

evidence.quote: a Sum not exceeding in the whole £1000
be addressed to Mr Darwin
their Lordships write immediately

record_reviews.summary: Darwin declines Elizabeth Wedgwood’s music-meeting invitation because he is working on proof sheets, describes plans to visit Shrewsbury and Maer, and reports family logistics around his father and Susan.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied single day [28 Aug 1837], with Monday Evening header.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes throughout; proof sheets, picture and travel arrangements are referenced objects/plans.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Much later Elizabeth incoming letter and different family situation; no connection.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Personal answer to an unlocated invitation; no candidate incoming source in this packet. The body answers an invitation but the originating Elizabeth letter is not preserved here.

evidence.quote: the infinite importance to a young author of his first proof sheets
What a waste of life to stop all summer in this ugly Marlborough Street
Yours affectionately | Chas Darwin

record_reviews.summary: Spearman communicates the Treasury’s approval of up to £1000 for Darwin’s publication, with conditions requiring an approved plan and certificates of engraving progress.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Safe single XML day 31 August 1837.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Spearman writes on behalf of the Lords Commissioners; this is a corporate administrative communication.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Preceding Treasury minute directs the immediate communication and contains the same £1000 conditions.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Direct official communication implementing 373A; no Darwin reply is present in this batch. The letter’s institutional route and wording directly correspond to the preceding Board minute.

evidence.quote: my Lords will feel themselves justified in giving their sanction
a sum, not exceeding in the whole one thousand pounds
A. Y. Spearman

record_reviews.summary: Children forwards Blyth’s accusation against George R. Gray and asks Darwin for an early character assessment based on Darwin’s use of the British Museum collections; the surviving text ends with the circular addressees.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Safe single XML day 21 February 1838.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Children writes as keeper of the zoological department; the enclosed Blyth letter is third-party material and the circular names multiple recipients.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Darwin’s next-day testimony explicitly answers Children’s subject and is the direct response.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Direct prompt to Darwin; paired outgoing answer is 402F. Darwin’s response must be limited to his own experience, not Blyth’s accusation or other circular recipients.

evidence.quote: a Copy of a Letter addressed to the Trustees
I request the favour of you to inform me
an early answer to which will much oblige

record_reviews.summary: Darwin answers Children’s character enquiry, reporting repeated courteous assistance from George Gray, ready access to cases and useful bibliographical guidance.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied single XML day 22 February 1838, with the dated closing; relationship to 402B establishes sequence.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes a personal testimony based on his own museum visits; no Blyth or Children prose is adopted as Darwin voice.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Children’s 21 February circular asks exactly for Darwin’s experience of Gray; direct subject and next-day sequence.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Direct response to Children’s surviving circular letter 402B. Only Darwin’s observed treatment is evidence; it does not resolve the wider accusation.

evidence.quote: Mr George Gray has uniformly acted towards me with courtesy
given me much useful information
February 22d.—

record_reviews.summary: Darwin answers Whitley’s personal letter, recalls Cambridge friends, announces his writing and Geological Society work, discusses his books and future marriage prospects, and declines the Newcastle meeting invitation.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied single day [8 May 1838], Tuesday night header.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes throughout; quotations from Herbert are reported speech, not Darwin voice.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Later outgoing Whitley letter also answers an unlocated Whitley letter, but distinct engagement/Glen Roy content prevents treating it as 411A’s response.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Answer to an unlocated Whitley letter; no incoming Whitley record is in the packet. The letter confirms an antecedent Whitley letter but not its contents or surviving ID.

evidence.quote: I was very glad the other day to receive your letter
I am turned a complete scribbler
your very kind invitation to pay you a visit

record_reviews.summary: Walker apologizes for delay, acknowledges Darwin’s suggestions about deficiencies in locality descriptions, discusses Chalcidites similarity across continents, and promises to borrow Darwin’s specimens and answer queries fully.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied single XML day 6 July 1838; year is bracketed in the title but XML resolves a single day.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Walker writes; Darwin’s specimens and queries are referenced as incoming materials/questions, not reproduced.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Later Walker answer to another request concerning Chalcidites; same correspondent and subject but no Darwin source identifies either prompt.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Directly answers an unlocated Darwin letter and promises a fuller specimen-based reply; no Darwin prompt survives. A response relationship to an absent Darwin request is explicit, but 421 cannot be paired to 721 solely by shared subject.

evidence.quote: answering your kind letter
your suggestions respecting the deficiencies
answer your queries fully

record_reviews.summary: Erasmus congratulates Darwin and Emma on their engagement, says he received Darwin’s letter and immediately shared the news, and plans to hear the details in person on Monday.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied single day [14 Nov 1838].
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Erasmus writes; “your letter” and the engagement news are reported receipt/context, with no embedded Darwin voice.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Darwin’s later engagement announcement to Whitley, but no evidence it answers Erasmus or is linked to this letter.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Acknowledges an unlocated Darwin engagement letter; no surviving Darwin reply is present. The personal plan to meet Monday does not establish a surviving written response.

evidence.quote: I received your letter just as I was going out
It is a marriage which will give almost as much pleasure
hear it all face to face

record_reviews.summary: Darwin announces his engagement to Whitley, describes Emma, their planned marriage and London life, discusses Glen Roy and Cambridge friends, and declines a northern invitation.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied single day 23 November 1838; the header supplies November 23d and XML gives a single day.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes throughout; references to Whitley’s letter and invitation are not reproduced.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Earlier Darwin letter to Whitley with different personal/scientific content; both answer unlocated Whitley correspondence.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Answer to an unlocated Whitley letter and invitation; no incoming Whitley text is preserved. The phrase “your letter” confirms prior receipt but cannot identify a packet record.

evidence.quote: I have been very long in answering your kind letter
I am glad to find from your letter that science is not so much at a discount
Most truly yrs, C. Darwin

record_reviews.summary: Darwin sends Stokes his Fungia observations, preserving comparisons with Actinia and Caryophyllia, and asks Stokes to improve style or anatomical names.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied bounded range [1839–September 1842] (1839-01-01 through 1842-09-30); exact day unresolved.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; the Fungia notes are his own voyage observations and the corals are referenced scientific materials.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Later Stokes administrative/scientific exchange about microscope and corals; no direct text links it as a reply.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Scientific submission to Stokes with no surviving Stokes prompt or response in the packet. Footnotes identify earlier advice and later corals but do not provide a surviving reply to 478.

evidence.quote: my few observations of Fungia
my comparisons with Actinia & Caryophyllia
make any improvements in style or names of parts

record_reviews.summary: Darwin tells the probable Shoberl recipient that FitzRoy approves advertising the Beagle-related works, asks him to consult Colburn, and clarifies the fly-page timing so binding is not delayed.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied single XML day [21 Mar 1839]. The date is conjectural from FitzRoy 500; the Thursday header and footnote preserve the uncertainty around publication route.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes to a conjecturally identified Shoberl; FitzRoy’s position is reported, while Colburn/Smith Elder are administrative third parties.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: FitzRoy’s 20 March incoming letter explicitly endorses advertising Zoology/Geology; 501 relays that position to the publisher intermediary, but is not addressed to FitzRoy.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Follow-up to FitzRoy’s surviving letter through Shoberl/Colburn; retain as candidate cross-recipient response rather than same-addressee reply. The content is highly distinctive, but the route is Darwin-to-Shoberl after FitzRoy-to-Darwin, so direct response status is conservative.

evidence.quote: Capt. FitzRoy has no kind of objection
the last day, I can send them
Chas. Darwin

record_reviews.summary: De Salis acknowledges Darwin’s notice of election as a Geological Society Fellow, encloses the signed obligation and subscription order, and asks Darwin to pass payment to the Treasurer.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Safe single XML day 8 July 1839.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: De Salis writes; the signed obligation and payment order are enclosures, and Darwin’s prior letter is referenced but absent.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Unrelated publication-advertisement administration.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Administrative response to Darwin’s unlocated election notice; no Darwin reply survives. The incoming letter proves a prior Darwin administrative notice but not its surviving text.

evidence.quote: your letter of the 23d Ult informing me of my Election
I beg to enclose the Obligation signed by me
Wm. Fane De Salis Charles Darwin Esqr

record_reviews.summary: An unidentified Edwards memorandum reports a setter puppy from apparently pure pointer parents, with the other puppies pointer-like, and says no remembered cross explains the reversion except a distant one.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied bounded date [before end of 1839?] (1839-01-01 through 1839-12-30); exact date and correspondent are unresolved.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Short incoming memorandum/fragment attributed only conjecturally to Mr Edwards; the Wilkins breeding account is a third-party report. It is not a Darwin transcription.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Darwin’s Jamaica animal questions are later and addressed to De la Beche; no direct source link.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Likely answers Darwin’s circulated breeding questionnaire, but the prompt and full letter are unlocated. The prose records a specific breeding observation but lacks a secure author/date and does not establish a direct surviving pair.

evidence.quote: threw one setter puppy
No cross was remembered and it must have been far back

record_reviews.summary: Darwin answers Walton’s guanaco enquiry with remembered slaughter weights, shipboard use and taste of the meat, while qualifying that the animals were lean and baked in a ship’s stove; he predicts better meat if domesticated and fattened.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied bounded range [1840–2] (1840-01-01 through 1842-12-31), dated by the Society for the Encouragement of Arts letter; exact day unresolved.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin-authored surviving answer text; quotation marks delimit the transcribed answer, not a catalogue abstract.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Parallel answer to Walton on guanaco range/tameness, but no incoming Walton text or internal reference distinguishes a shared prompt.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Answer to an unlocated Walton enquiry; no surviving incoming letter is present. The content is a substantive Darwin answer, but the prompt and receipt route are absent.

evidence.quote: answering, as far as lies in my power, your enquiries regarding the guanaco
served out on board H. M. ship Beagle as fresh meat
if domesticated and fattened

record_reviews.summary: Darwin answers Walton on guanaco ecology and domestication, surveying deserts, snowline, Patagonia, La Plata and Tierra del Fuego, then noting no regional difference and the ease with which young guanacos become tame.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied bounded range [1840–2] (1840-01-01 through 1842-12-31), using the same Society letter as dating basis; exact day unresolved.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin-authored surviving answer text; the geographic observations are Darwin’s Beagle experience.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Same addressee and subject, but a separate answer text without a surviving prompt or internal cross-reference.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Answer to an unlocated Walton enquiry; no direct incoming source survives. Shared guanaco topic and date range do not prove 548A and 548B are parts of one letter or responses to each other.

evidence.quote: Perhaps there is no animal in the world
I could perceive no difference in the guanacos of these several regions
the guanaco so easily becomes tame

record_reviews.summary: Abberley reports seed outcomes for peas, beans, thyme and insect-pollinated cucumbers, including a possible bean mule and a successful hand-dusted cucumber. R. W. Darwin says he read and redirects Abberley’s conclusions, with more to follow.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Safe single XML day 18 October 1841.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Joint incoming text: Abberley supplies pp.1–7 in rough spelling; R. W. Darwin writes p.8 and signs p.9. Neither is Darwin C.R.; the seed observations and notebook footnote are distinct from a CD-authored prompt.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Both concern inherited variation, but 13803 is an unidentified earlier breeding memorandum and no direct connection is stated.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Incoming household experiment report; no surviving Darwin C.R. response is present. R.W. Darwin’s transmission establishes that he read the gardener’s text, not that CD received or authored it; the report is not a Darwin voice exception.

evidence.quote: the insects carred Pollen
Abberly has just given me the above letter to read
Your affecti— father | R W D 18 Oct 41

record_reviews.summary: Darwin returns Stokes’s snuff box, sends an antique microscope with a repair memorandum for Powell, and sends corals to be left until they can meet.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied bounded range [Jan–Mar 1842] (1842-01-01 through 1842-03-31); exact day unresolved despite Wednesday Evening header.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; snuff box, microscope, memorandum and corals are physical objects. Powell is the proposed repairer, not the letter’s recipient.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Earlier scientific Fungia submission to Stokes, but no direct response text or exact ordering connects the records.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Administrative/scientific follow-up to prior Stokes exchange with no surviving Stokes input in the packet. Footnotes mention earlier coral advice and a later account entry, but neither is a surviving direct prompt.

evidence.quote: my dear old antique microscope with a memorandum within for Mr. Powell
I send my corals
Yours most truly | C. Darwin

record_reviews.summary: Darwin sends De la Beche four structured questions about inherited variation in Jamaican horses, cattle, dogs, cats, poultry, pigs, goats and sheep, including tameness, crossbreeding and wool deterioration.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Safe single XML day 7 February 1842; signed/date paragraph and address are explicit.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes all four questions; De la Beche’s Jamaican experience is requested, not supplied.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Earlier unidentified breeding report, but no Jamaican subject or direct response.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Initiating questionnaire; no De la Beche response survives in the packet. The detailed prompt is usable for future matching, but no incoming answer is available.

evidence.quote: What colour are the horses
if crossed with ordinary tame breeds
deterioration in the character of the wool

record_reviews.summary: Elizabeth reports the serious illness of Josiah Wedgwood, arranges transport for Mrs Bennett, comments on Emma’s distress and the birth of a daughter, and hopes Catherine can go.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied single XML day [25 Sept 1842].
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Elizabeth writes; the “good news” and birth reference Darwin’s unlocated 23 September letter, not Darwin voice.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Same-date Hensleigh family letter is a separate incoming text; no direct response relationship.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Acknowledges an unlocated Darwin family letter announcing Mary Eleanor’s birth; no surviving Darwin response here. The footnote identifies the prior Darwin letter only by date, not by an available record ID.

evidence.quote: the good news your letter brings
My poor dear Emma what sad news to meet her after her labour
I am very glad it is a little girl

record_reviews.summary: Darwin congratulates Davis on returning from the Antarctic expedition, recalls a letter sent to Rio de Janeiro and Davis’s specimen gift, arranges return or sorting of Davis’s box, and discusses Beagle shipmates and Hooker.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied single XML day 15 September 1843; Down address and September 15 header are explicit, with bracketed year component.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; specimens and box are physical materials, and the Rio letter is an unlocated earlier Darwin letter.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Later Covington letter shares Beagle news but is a separate addressee and relationship.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Follow-up to Davis’s return and an unlocated Rio letter; no incoming Davis source is in the packet. The reference to the Rio letter proves prior correspondence but does not identify a surviving prompt or Davis receipt date.

evidence.quote: I hope you received my letter sent to Rio de Janeiro
Your Box is at my Brothers lodgings
write to me about your Specimens

record_reviews.summary: Darwin sends Covington a new ear trumpet as a present through Smith Elder’s correspondent Evans, reports his health, children, publications and Beagle news, and acknowledges Covington’s last letter and will.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Safe single XML day 7 October 1843.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; ear trumpet and shipping box are physical objects, and Covington’s last letter is referenced but absent.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Earlier Davis letter about a different returning expedition and specimens; shared Beagle history is not a direct link.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Personal/material response to an unlocated Covington letter; no incoming Covington source is present. The explicit last-letter reference establishes prior receipt in principle, but no surviving prompt or actual date of Darwin’s receipt is available.

evidence.quote: Your new ear-trumpet has gone by the ship Sultana
I was glad to get your last letter
The Zoology of the voyage of the Beagle is also completed

record_reviews.summary: Walker apologizes for delaying his answer to Darwin’s Chalcidites request, compares most localities with European forms, identifies distinct Australian/Brazilian/Galápagos forms, and notes Darwin’s specimens are safely deposited in the British Museum.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Safe single XML day 10 December 1843.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Walker writes; taxonomic claims and specimen status are Walker’s answer and observations, not Darwin voice.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Earlier Walker response to a different locality-description request; same taxon and author but no surviving Darwin text ties them.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Direct response to an unlocated Darwin request; no matching Darwin source is in the packet. “Your request” is explicit, but the requested letter and date of receipt are absent.

evidence.quote: answering your request for information
your Chalcidites are safely deposited in the British Museum
quite distinct from any of Europe

record_reviews.summary: Darwin tells Cresy that Hooker thanks him for offering a plant but does not want it, explaining that Hooker’s workload delayed his reply. Darwin says this answers two or three of his own letters.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Period-held alternative-date record: 26 December 1843–April 1846, or September 1855–October 1860 (XML 1843-12-26 through 1860-10-26); exact year and date unresolved.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; Hooker’s reported thanks are indirect speech. The plant and unlocated letters are missing context, so the surviving text is a short fragment/letter with unresolved chronology.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Unrelated Darwin questionnaire to De la Beche; no plant or Hooker overlap.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Response to two or three unlocated Darwin letters via Hooker; no surviving Cresy/Hooker prompt is present. The body confirms multiple prior Darwin letters and a plant offer but neither their IDs nor actual receipt date.

evidence.quote: In answer to 2 or 3 letters of mine
offer of plant
he really could not write before

proposed_links.reason: The Board minute orders an immediate communication to Darwin; Spearman’s dated letter is that communication and repeats the same £1000 publication conditions. This is an official follow-on, not a Darwin-authored reply.

evidence.quote: be addressed to Mr Darwin
My Lords have therefore directed me to communicate to you the views they entertain

proposed_links.reason: Children’s circular asks Darwin for his own experience of Gray; Darwin’s next-day letter directly reports that Gray acted courteously and provided access and information.

evidence.quote: I request the favour of you to inform me
With respect to the subject of your letter
Mr George Gray has uniformly acted towards me with courtesy

proposed_links.reason: Darwin’s next-day letter to the publisher intermediary relays FitzRoy’s distinctive advertising approval and asks for implementation. The cross-recipient route means this is a follow-up based on 500 rather than a same-addressee direct reply.

evidence.quote: every reason for my wishing that an advertisement of the Zoology
Capt. FitzRoy has no kind of objection
what is the last day, I can send them

issues.description: All 24 batch-16 records, all retained body paragraphs, headers, summaries and editorial notes were read in full.

No batch-16 paragraph was merely a bracketed catalogue abstract like the known 13864 case. DCP-LETT-13803 is nevertheless a short unidentified memorandum/fragment, and DCP-LETT-548A/B are retained Darwin answer texts with quotation punctuation.
DCP-LETT-344 and DCP-LETT-610 are multi-author/joint texts; DCP-LETT-373A and 377 are corporate Treasury documents; third-party reports/quotations remain attributed to their original speakers.

Editorially supplied single days were retained as provenance; bounded/alternative dates for 478, 501, 548A/B and 13787 remain unresolved, and no receipt date was inferred from composition or publication context.

DCP-LETT-402B encloses Blyth’s letter, DCP-LETT-501 references FitzRoy/Colburn publication material, DCP-LETT-525 encloses an obligation/order, DCP-LETT-610 transmits household notes, and several source prompts are unlocated.
